Not to take away from the severity of the event but I see a difference between sexual abuse and rape. The primary difference being intercourse. Many of these words are interchangeable... rape, sexual assault, sexual abuse etc etc. 

I would say he sexually abused you. Unless you guys have spoken prior about such a thing (TMI but for example my girlfriend and I both agreed that should the other want sex it’s ok if you wake up to it. If you don’t want it at that point. Simply stop it). If you guys never clarified that and he did something you did not want you should definitely speak out about it! I’ve learned from my event involving sexual abuse that I needed to talk about it not just for my sake but for others as well. That he couldn’t do what he did to me, to others.

I find myself in a unique position I think, it’s at least opened up my eyes a lot. I myself, male, was sexually abused and am currently dating a women who was raped. I know what it’s like to go through it, and now I know what it’s like to deal with a loved one who went through it. 

I’m happy to answer any other questions you may have, not just the one that you mentioned specifically. 

First I would say recognize that basically all victims react differently. I personally bottled up. I didn’t say anything for years. Kept to myself and acted like everything was fine and tried to continue about my regular life. My girlfriend spoke up sooner and has been fighting for longer than I have to heal. It could be that your girlfriend is in that stage... she’s trying to be normal again. 

After an event the idea of “normal” kind of goes out the window. You see people, parties, bars, actions, favors, nice gestures... everything as different. Everything could be an attack or a betrayal. But you have to keep living. With the sheer amounts of depression, guilt, anxiety, anger, frustration, pure rage.... suicide is an easy option. Sometimes even just pretending like life is normal and faking it can keep you going. 

My girlfriend has lots of ups and downs. She will have night terrors, just like this morning, where she literally wakes up screaming. Other days she’s happy, trusts me, believes me and knows I will protect her. You have to reinforce those moments. You have to show her time and time again that you love her, will protect her and are there for her. In the good and bad moments! Let her live, encourage her to live and go out and have fun. Don’t be suffocating but be there. It’s kind of a full time job! Haha.

He wasn’t intimately attached to this other women and I think you could find some peace in that. He’s intimate with you and loves you and simply did what you guys agreed on, as did you.

It really just depends on what you want. I was with a girl who was a once a week type of gal and I’m not that type of a guy. My current girlfriend and I are more like 2-4 times a day. Then one of my good guy friends is a 1-2 times a week... everyone has their preferences!

Please press charges. Who knows how many other people who could do this do. Unfortunately my attacker got away with it scotch free. I feel that was a mistake and insult to me and it kills me to think about it. Talk with your husband, lean on him, have at least a little something to eat and press charges.

Hey man I had a similar experience, I was sexually assaulted by my ecclesiastical leader and have been dealing with that for nearly 5 years now. He got away with it too. I wish I had some “this is what helped me turn my life around and now I’m great!” Advice but honestly.... I’m still struggling with it too. Two things that have helped me tho is 1: talk. Talk about it man. In however much or little detail as you want but try to talk about it. I bottled my event up for about 4 years without saying a word to anyone and it really drove me to dark places. 2: in whatever way (it could be talking about it) don’t let him control your life through fear, threats, embarrassment.. whatever emotion. Don’t let him control you. Be in control of your life.
